editorial:
Imagine your favorite cool, calm stuntman from the sixties stepping into a world that has moved on without him. You get to follow Cliff Booth as he navigates a new version of Los Angeles where he is now the guy people call to clean up their biggest messes. The vibe is a perfect mix of a gritty crime story and a dark comedy. You will love how Cliff stays totally relaxed while everything around him is falling apart. It feels like a high-stakes game of cat and mouse where the prize is just staying alive in a city full of fake people and dangerous secrets.

Everything about the movie hits the mark, especially the way the mystery unfolds with a few shocks you won't see coming. The acting is top-notch, and the action scenes are snappy and realistic. If you find the middle part a bit slow, just stick with it because the finale is wild. It is a great pick for anyone who likes a smart crime flick with a lot of heart.
endingExplained: In the final act, you find out that the studio boss was actually the one framing Cliff for the murders. Cliff uses his old stuntman tricks to trap the boss in a fake movie set, making him confess on a live feed. After a quick fight, Cliff hands the evidence to the police and walks away. He ends the movie by driving his car toward the coast, finally leaving the Hollywood mess behind for good.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves cool protagonists and twisty crime stories.
